subject: Eval debrief: Redwood vs Hyperscaler — side-by-side test request
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orchid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Eval debrief: Redwood vs Hyperscaler — side-by-side test request

Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a concrete request for the side-by-side tests we discussed.

High-level takeaways from the demo/discovery:
- Orcid will prioritize low-latency streaming for multi-turn assistants and a predictable per-token cost for high-volume batch jobs.
- Your engineering constraints: region = us-west, strict PII handling, and a 3rd-party KMS requirement for any private deployments.
- Primary hyperscaler concerns: model access variability and the orchestration complexity for mixed workloads (streaming + batch).

Where Redwood differentiates (short):
1) Consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private with model pinning and rollout controls.
2) Streaming + function/tool calling that preserves partial structured outputs (we can stream JSON fragments safely).
3) Cost controls: intelligent batching + quantization profiles tuned per workload.
4) Smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants during capacity spikes.

Requested side-by-side tests (what we propose Redwood run vs. your hyperscaler baseline):
A) Streaming fidelity: identical prompt set of ~40 multi-turn conversations (avg 6 turns). Measure first-token latency, median token latency, and correctness of streamed JSON chunks for function calls.
B) Function calling / tool invocation: 25 prompts that require structured tool arguments (dates, amounts, entity ids). Validate exactness of parsed args and error rates.
C) Structured output tolerance: prompts expected to produce strict JSON/CSV outputs; compute schema-valid success rate.
D) Throughput & cost: batch run of 1M tokens generated across small/medium/large model variants; report throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, and per-token cost estimate after quantization.

Success metrics / SLAs for the tests:
- Streaming first-token P50 < 250ms, P95 < 700ms (us-west test bed)
- Function calling schema success >= 98% on exact-match fields
- Structured-output schema pass >= 99%
- Per-token cost delta vs hyperscaler <= 20% (for comparable latency)

Practical asks from you to run the hyperscaler side:
- Provide a representative prompt set (we can anonymize) or confirm we use the set from today's call.
- Confirm environment details (region, model family/version, quantization enabled?).
- Point us at any internal constraints doc we should respect (IAM/KMS/network).

I've attached a proposed test matrix (redwood-test-matrix.xlsx) and a short SLA summary (redwood-sla-summary.pdf). Proposed window to run tests: next Wednesday–Friday (2026-07-07 to 2026-07-09).

Next steps: if you confirm the prompt set + constraints, Marissa (SE) will schedule the runs and share the exact bench harness. After runs we'll do a focused 45-min results review and recommend configuration changes.

Thanks — looking forward to making the comparison concrete.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-test-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, test cases), redwood-sla-summary.pdf (one-pager)

Rishi — thanks for the clear recap. Priya and I reviewed the test plan and overall this aligns with what we need to evaluate. A couple of clarifications and constraints from our side:

1) Prompt set: we'll provide the 40 multi-turn threads you mentioned but need to scrub customer PII. We'll deliver a redacted .json by Monday EOD (2026-07-05).
2) Hyperscaler baseline: we'll run the baseline on our committed endpoint (g1.large-family) with native streaming enabled and no quantization (for fairness). We can enable 4-bit quant later as a separate pass.
3) KMS: we cannot share keys but will provide an access pattern doc. If Redwood requires KMS interactions, we need to map them to our SOC controls first. See attached: orchid-internal-constraints.pdf.

One small ask: can Redwood include a test variant where function-calling outputs are intentionally chunked (partial JSON) to simulate early flushes? That was a common failure mode for us on prior tests.

Thanks — we'll aim to upload the prompt set Monday and schedule a 30-min sync Tuesday to lock the harness.

—Samir
CTO | Orchid AI

Samir / Rishi — Marissa (SE) here. Thanks for the confirmation, Samir. A few technical notes and the exact harness we'll run so you know what's measured end-to-end.

Harness summary (what Redwood will run):
- Runner: open-source bench harness (internal fork) that emits the prompt set with deterministic seeds.
- Streaming test: we will capture token-level timestamps, partial payloads, and function-call boundary markers. We'll also compute a "stream integrity" score that measures if partial JSON chunks can be reassembled without schema errors.
- Function-calling fidelity: we will run two parsers — Redwood's strict schema validator and a relaxed parser that tolerates ordering differences. We'll report both exact-match and tolerant-match rates.
- Quantization pass: runs for 8-bit (float16 baseline) and 4-bit (GPTQ-style) with model-family specific kernels.

Data & infra asks from your side:
- Delivered prompt set (redacted)
- Hyperscaler endpoint + model name (string), and the region used for the baseline run (us-west preferred)
- Any rate-limit rules we should respect so we don't trigger false throttling

Timing & artifacts:
- We'll provide raw logs, aggregated metrics CSV, and a human-readable results deck within 48 hours of finishing the runs.
- Test window can be Jul 7–9 as Rishi proposed; please confirm Tue Jul 6 if you want a pre-run sync so SEs can align.

Attachment: se-test-config.json (this is a stub with exact flags we'll use).

If you want, we can also include a small canary run during the week (10 conversations) to validate the harness before full runs. Recommend doing that Tues afternoon.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
